headlines.text: Flash back to 2026, when a new champion was crowned for the AEW World Heavyweight Title as Kenny Omega vs. MJF battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 9.17 ? a war that left everything in the ring ? ending the champion's reign at 3 defenses. It marked Kenny Omega's 10th match with the title on the line. In a match where a loss meant Omega could never challenge for the title again, he survived a low blow and a shot with his own belt before landing three V-Triggers and a One-Winged Angel to dethrone MJF and become a two-time AEW World Champion.
Back on this day in 2023, CM Punk vs. Samoa Joe met in a Tournament Match, closing out the card as the main event on Collision, rated 7.61 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle.

Rewind to 2020, when The Lucha Brothers vs. The Butcher and The Blade vs. FTR vs. The Young Bucks vs. Pentagon Jr. vs. Rey Fenix vs. The Butcher vs. The Blade vs. Cash Wheeler vs. Dax Harwood vs. Matt Jackson vs. Nick Jackson delivered a real highlight of the night on Dynamite, rated 8.37 ? part of that year's Fyter Fest '20 - Night 2.

secondaries.text: Looking back to 2022, when Eddie Kingston vs. Konosuke Takeshita delivered a hard-hitting, high-quality battle on Rampage, rated 8.02.

It was 2026 when the AEW International Title changed hands as Kyle Fletcher vs. Konosuke Takeshita battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.37 ? an excellent showing ? ending the champion's reign at 3 defenses. Konosuke Takeshita was chasing gold for the 10th time. With timely interference from Don Callis, Fletcher brought the International Championship "home" to the Don Callis Family, defeating his own stablemate Takeshita on the same historic night Omega won the world title.
Looking back to 2023, when Bullet Club Gold vs. FTR met in an Eliminator Match on Collision, rated 8.70 ? a war that left everything in the ring.
